open_questions: Transit duration 1.743 h vs central 1.14 h ratio 1.53 and star_density_penalty 232.2 remain unexplained by a central planet – consistent with spot crossings but need spot-modelling or out-of-transit photometry to confirm

Sector-to-sector depth changes (496 ppm to 55 ppm) are large even in TESS-SPOC – remaining uncertainty is whether NEB correction/spot contamination fully accounts for it; ground-based high-resolution transit photometry in a single season would test
dossier.public_summary: TESS finds a flat-bottomed 290 ppm dip every 0.56 day on the target star itself, with no sign of a second eclipse or alternating depths and a size of about 1.3 Earth radii. The star is strongly spotted with the same 0.56-day rotation period, producing a large phase-curve swing that makes the dip depth appear to change between sectors, but that activity explains the variability, not a background binary. The signal is therefore best explained as an ultra-short-period planet synchronised to its host star’s spin.

reasons.why: Dip is localized on the target; no neighbour within 1 pixel (21 arcsec) can plausibly fake the 290 ppm dip, and suspects are 3.6 sigma or more from the centroid. Rules out a blended neighbour EB.
reasons.value: on_target offset 12.21 arcsec err 11.01 arcsec offset_sigma 1.109, neighbours plausible_within_1px 0

reasons.why: Flat-bottomed (-4.235) transit of planet size (1.255 Re, rp/rstar 0.01738) with no secondary (snr 2.561) and no odd/even difference (diff_sigma 0.6574). Positively favours a planet over a V-shaped EB/grazer.

Dip is at exactly the stellar rotation period, strong sign of variability. BUT strong variability alone is not evidence against a planet: RV amplitude 3.574 is stellar rotation modulation (spin-orbit resynchronised ultra-short-period planet), and fit density mismatch (star_density_penalty 232.2, duration ratio 1.53, fit_k 0.01439) is caused by large spot crossings and phase curve, not a binary. No secondary, no odd/even, flat shape and planet size keep planet as best explanation; variability is expected for a USP on an active K-dwarf.
reasons.value: rotation amplitude 1293-1414 ppm, phase_curve amplitude_ppm 237.5 ratio_to_depth 0.8191 chi2 113.2/7, signal period 0.56 d vs rotation 0.561 d

reasons.why: Depth changes between sectors even within the same pipeline, argued against by xgboost planet_rank 0.19, but changes are expected when spot modulation (1414 ppm vs 290 ppm transit) biases out-of-transit baseline and transit depth. Odd/even, secondary and centroid checks are all planet-like, so the confirmed spot period and large phase curve are identified as stellar activity, not an EB. Similar checks are all planet outcomes.
